correctness.rationale: Pass is for the complete replacement repairs/2/RESULT.md. Frozen Step 4, line 57, did not justify its key globalization: properness does not confine a free family of bounded-length loops. For instance a complete proper hyperbolic cusp cylinder has arbitrarily short essential circles and no closed geodesic; in metric du²+e^(2u)dθ², periodic u along a geodesic would force u''=e^(2u)θ'²=0 and then zero velocity. This invalidates the proposed general inference, not the obstacle theorem. The replacement verifies Bowditch directly: inverse Gauss coordinates give d(log t)²+|(I+B/t)dω|² with B positive, so truncating t upward does not increase length. A projected loop of length ell<2pi sits in a hemisphere (for two half-arclength points a,b, every x has d(a,x)+d(b,x)<=ell/2, giving x·(a+b)>0). The round radial contraction is nonexpanding there, and at sufficiently large fixed t its lifted length is bounded by (1+sup||B||/t)ell, at most the original length because ell is strictly smaller for nonconstant projections. The constant projection case contracts by truncation alone. All short loops are therefore in one component. Independently checked: conformal curvature follows from the principal-distance Hessian and |∇t|=1; the exact geodesic log identity has the asserted sign; quasihyperbolic balls are compact by the exponential bounds; smooth outer approximants arise by rotational smoothing of support functions plus a small ball; compact-uniform distance convergence and radial retreat into slightly smaller balls yield pointed GH convergence and preserve CAT(1). The ball tangent curvatures tend to 1 in n>=3. The frozen 510 rational assertions were inspected, not rerun, and do not certify globalization or the limit argument.
